source_doc: ICMR Standard Treatment Workflows: Essential Hypertension
content: In patients with diabetes mellitus and hypertension, ACE inhibitors (such as Enalapril) or ARBs (such as Telmisartan) are first-line agents due to renal protective effects. Beta-blockers should be used with caution as they can mask hypoglycemic symptoms (tachycardia, tremor). Calcium channel blockers (Amlodipine) can be combined if monotherapy is insufficient.

source_doc: ICMR Standard Treatment Workflows: Oral Anticoagulation Management
section: Section 5.1 - Warfarin Monitoring and NSAID Interactions
content: Target INR for non-valvular atrial fibrillation is 2.0 - 3.0. Concomitant use of NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac) or Aspirin significantly elevates upper GI bleeding risk. NSAIDs must be avoided; Paracetamol (up to 2g/day) is recommended for analgesia. INR must be re-checked 3 days after introducing any new systemic antibiotic or antifungal.

source_doc: ICMR Standard Treatment Workflows: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
content: Metformin is the first-line pharmacotherapy for Type 2 Diabetes. Check eGFR prior to initiation. Metformin is contraindicated if eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2. Dose reduction by 50% is required if eGFR is between 30 and 45 mL/min/1.73m2. Temporarily withhold Metformin 48 hours prior to iodinated radiocontrast imaging procedures to prevent lactic acidosis.

source_doc: WHO Guidelines: Pharmacological Management of Cardiac Emergencies
content: Sublingual or intravenous Nitroglycerin/Isosorbide mononitrate causes severe, irreversible vasodilatory hypotension if co-administered with PDE-5 inhibitors (Sildenafil, Tadalafil, Vardenafil). Administration of nitrates within 24 hours of Sildenafil or 48 hours of Tadalafil is strictly contraindicated in acute coronary syndrome.

source_doc: ICMR Standard Treatment Workflows: Acute Bronchial Asthma
section: Section 2.3 - Red Flag Symptoms & Emergency Escalation
content: Red flag symptoms requiring immediate intensive care / emergency escalation include: Silent chest on auscultation, inability to complete full sentences in one breath, cyanosis, altered mental state, respiratory rate > 30/min, or PEFR < 33% predicted. Immediate administration of high-flow oxygen, inhaled SABA (Salbutamol) via nebulizer, and IV hydrocortisone is mandatory.

source_doc: ICMR Guidelines: Antimicrobial Stewardship & Quinolone Safety
section: Section 6.2 - Quinolone Drug Interactions & QT Prolongation
content: Fluoroquinolones (Ciprofloxacin, Levofloxacin, Moxifloxacin) inhibit CYP1A2 and cause QT interval prolongation. Concomitant use with Tizanidine is strictly contraindicated due to severe hypotension and CNS depression. Co-administration with Amiodarone or Sotalol increases risk of Torsades de Pointes arrhythmia.

source_doc: ICMR Standard Treatment Workflows: Peptic Ulcer Disease & PPI Interactions
section: Section 3.1 - Proton Pump Inhibitors & Clopidogrel Efficacy
content: Omeprazole and Esomeprazole competitively inhibit CYP2C19, decreasing the conversion of Clopidogrel to its active antiplatelet metabolite. Pantoprazole or Rabeprazole exhibit lower CYP2C19 affinity and are preferred acid suppressants for cardiac patients on Clopidogrel therapy.

source_doc: ICMR Standard Treatment Workflows: Epilepsy and Anticonvulsants
content: Phenytoin exhibits non-linear zero-order therapeutic pharmacokinetics. Hepatic enzyme inducers (Carbamazepine, Rifampicin) lower serum Phenytoin levels. Sodium Valproate displaces Phenytoin from plasma protein binding sites while inhibiting its metabolism, leading to acute phenytoin toxicity (nystagmus, ataxia).

source_doc: ICMR National TB Elimination Program: Anti-TB Drug Safety
section: Section 7.1 - Rifampicin Enzyme Induction & Oral Contraceptives
content: Rifampicin is a potent inducer of hepatic CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. It dramatically accelerates the metabolism of oral contraceptives, Warfarin, HIV protease inhibitors, and Oral Antidiabetics (Glimepiride). Alternative non-hormonal contraception and serial INR/blood glucose monitoring are mandatory during TB treatment.

Maximum daily dose of Paracetamol in adults is 4.0 grams/day (reduced to 2.0g/day in chronic alcoholism or underlying liver cirrhosis). Overdose leads to NAPQI metabolite accumulation causing centrilobular hepatic necrosis. Early administration of IV N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) within 8 hours prevents irreversible hepatic failure.

source_doc: WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children: Fever Management
section: Section 4.2 - Pediatric Fever & Aspirin Reye Syndrome Warning
content: Aspirin is strictly contraindicated in infants and children under 16 years of age presenting with viral infections (influenza, varicella/chickenpox) due to the fatal risk of Reye's Syndrome (acute encephalopathy and fatty liver failure). Paracetamol (10-15 mg/kg per dose) is the safe antipyretic of choice.

source_doc: ICMR Guidelines: Dosing Guidelines in Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)
section: Section 5.4 - NSAID Induced Acute Kidney Injury
content: NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Diclofenac, Naproxen, Ketorolac) inhibit renal prostaglandin synthesis, causing afferent arteriolar constriction and acute renal hypoperfusion. NSAIDs are contraindicated in patients with eGFR < 30 mL/min, volume depletion, severe heart failure, or co-prescribed ACE-I + Diuretics (Triple Whammy risk).

source_doc: ICMR Standard Treatment Workflows: Major Depressive Disorder
section: Section 3.5 - Serotonin Syndrome Warning with SSRIs and MAOIs
content: Concomitant administration of SSRIs (Fluoxetine, Sertraline) or SNRIs with MAO inhibitors (Selegiline, Linezolid antibiotic) triggers Serotonin Syndrome characterized by hyperthermia, neuromuscular agitation, rigidity, and autonomic instability. A 14-day wash-out period is mandatory when switching agents.

Levothyroxine (T4) must be taken on an empty stomach 30-60 minutes before breakfast. Calcium carbonate, Iron supplements (Ferrous Sulfate), Aluminum hydroxide antacids, and Sucralfate bind to Levothyroxine in the GI tract, reducing thyroid hormone absorption by over 50%. Separate dosing by at least 4 hours.

source_doc: ICMR Guidelines: Systemic Cancer Chemotherapy Safety
content: NSAIDs and Penicillins diminish renal tubular secretion of Methotrexate, resulting in elevated serum methotrexate levels, profound bone marrow suppression, severe mucositis, and acute renal tubular necrosis. Concomitant high-dose NSAID therapy with Methotrexate is strictly contraindicated.
